sentences.zh: 英宗九子。

translations.literal: The Yingzong Emperor had nine sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingzong Emperor had nine sons.

sentences.zh: 憲宗外，庶三子見湜未封，殤。

translations.literal: Apart from Xianzong, three sons by secondary consorts—Jian Shi among them—were not enfeoffed and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Besides the future Xianzong Emperor, three sons born to secondary consorts, including Jian Shi, were never enfeoffed and died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 其得封者七王，曰德莊王見潾，曰許悼王見淳，曰秀懷王見澍，曰崇簡王見澤，曰吉簡王見浚，曰忻穆王見治，曰徽莊王見沛。

translations.literal: Those who received enfeoffment were seven princes: Prince Zhuang of De, Jian Lin; Prince Dao of Xu, Jian Chun; Prince Huai of Xiu, Jian Shu; Prince Jian of Chong, Jian Ze; Prince Jian of Ji, Jian Jun; Prince Mu of Xin, Jian Zhi; and Prince Zhuang of Hui, Jian Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Seven received princely titles: Zhu Jianlin as Prince Zhuang of De; Zhu Jianchun as Prince Dao of Xu; Zhu Jianshu as Prince Huai of Xiu; Zhu Jianze as Prince Jian of Chong; Zhu Jianjun as Prince Jian of Ji; Zhu Jianzhi as Prince Mu of Xin; and Zhu Jianpei as Prince Zhuang of Hui.

sentences.zh: rowspan="16" valign="top"|德 莊王見潾，英宗庶二子，天順元年封。成化三年就藩濟南府。正德十二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang of De, Jian Lin, the Yingzong Emperor's second son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianshun. In the third year of Chenghua he went to his fief at Jinan Prefecture. He died in the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhuang of De, Zhu Jianlin, the Yingzong Emperor's second son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in 1457. He took up residence at his fief in Jinan Prefecture in 1467 and died in 1517.

sentences.zh: 懿王祐榕，莊嫡二子，正德十六年襲封。嘉靖十八年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Yi, You Rong, the Zhuang prince's second son by the principal consort, succeeded to the title in the sixteenth year of Zhengde and died in the eighteenth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi, Zhu Yourong, second son of the principal consort of Prince Zhuang of De, inherited the title in 1521 and died in 1539.

sentences.zh: 厚燉，懿庶二子，初封東平王，嘉靖中改封世子。未幾卒。以子載墱襲封，追封王，諡曰懷。

translations.literal: Hou Dun, the Yi's second son by a secondary consort, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping and in the Jiajing reign was changed to heir apparent. Before long he died. His son Zai Qiang succeeded; he was posthumously enfeoffed as a prince with the posthumous title Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hodun, Prince Yi's second son by a secondary consort, was first made Prince of Dongping and later named heir apparent during the Jiajing reign. He died soon afterward. His son Zhu Zaiqiang inherited the line; Hodun was posthumously raised to princely rank with the posthumous title Huai.

sentences.zh: 恭王載墱，懷庶二子，嘉靖二十年襲封。萬曆二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Gong, Zai Qiang, the Huai prince's second son by a secondary consort, succeeded in the twentieth year of Jiajing and died in the second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong, Zhu Zaiqiang, second son by a secondary consort of the posthumously titled Prince Huai, succeeded in 1541 and died in 1574.

sentences.zh: 定王翊錧，恭嫡一子，萬曆五年襲封。十六年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Ding, Yi Kan, the Gong prince's only son by the principal consort, succeeded in the fifth year of Wanli and died in the sixteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ding, Zhu Yikan, the Gong prince's only son by the principal consort, inherited the title in 1577 and died in 1588.

sentences.zh: 王常〈⿱邦清〉，定嫡一子，萬曆十九年襲封。崇禎五年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Chang, the Ding prince's only son by the principal consort (his name was written with a rare variant graph), succeeded in the nineteenth year of Wanli and died in the fifth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhu Chang, whose personal name used a rare variant character, the Ding prince's only son by the principal consort, succeeded in 1591 and died in 1632.

sentences.zh: 由𣒻，常〈⿱邦清〉庶一子，初封廣宗王，萬曆四十三年改封世子。未襲，卒。 王由樞，常〈⿱邦清〉庶二子，初封郡王，崇禎中進封。十二年正月，大清兵克濟南，見執。

translations.literal: You Nie, the Chang prince's first son by a secondary consort, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Guangzong and in the forty-third year of Wanli was changed to heir apparent; before succeeding he died. Prince You Shu, the Chang prince's second son by a secondary consort, was first enfeoffed as a commandery prince and was advanced during Chongzhen. In the first month of the twelfth year, Qing forces captured Jinan and he was taken prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Younie, first son by a secondary consort of Prince Chang, was first made Prince of Guangzong and named heir apparent in 1615 but died before he could succeed. Prince Zhu Youshu, the second son by a secondary consort, was first enfeoffed as a commandery prince and later promoted during the Chongzhen reign. In the first month of 1639 Qing troops took Jinan and captured him.

sentences.zh: 其得封者十王，曰興獻王祐杬，曰岐惠王祐棆，曰益端王祐檳，曰衡恭王祐楎，曰雍靖王祐橒，曰壽定王祐榰，曰汝定王祐梈，曰涇簡王祐橓，曰榮莊王祐樞，曰申懿王祐楷。

translations.literal: Those who received enfeoffment were ten princes: Prince Xian of Xing, You Yuan; Prince Hui of Qi, You Lun; Prince Duan of Yi, You Bin; Prince Gong of Heng, You Wei; Prince Jing of Yong, You Yuan; Prince Ding of Shou, You Zhi; Prince Ding of Ru, You Bing; Prince Jian of Jing, You Chuan; Prince Zhuang of Rong, You Shu; and Prince Yi of Shen, You Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Ten received princely titles: Zhu Youyuan as Prince Xian of Xing; Zhu Youlun as Prince Hui of Qi; Zhu Youbin as Prince Duan of Yi; Zhu Youwei as Prince Gong of Heng; Zhu Youyuan as Prince Jing of Yong; Zhu Youzhi as Prince Ding of Shou; Zhu Youbing as Prince Ding of Ru; Zhu Youchuan as Prince Jian of Jing; Zhu Youshu as Prince Zhuang of Rong; and Zhu Youkai as Prince Yi of Shen.

sentences.zh: 興 獻王祐杬，憲宗庶四子，成化二十三年封。弘治七年就藩安陸州。正德十四年薨。後以子嗣大統，追尊獻皇帝，廟號睿宗。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Xing, You Yuan, the Xianzong Emperor's fourth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in the twenty-third year of Chenghua. In the seventh year of Hongzhi he went to his fief at Anlu Subprefecture. He died in the fourteenth year of Zhengde. Later, because his son succeeded to the Great Succession, he was posthumously honored as the Xian Emperor with the temple name Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Xing, Zhu Youyuan, the Xianzong Emperor's fourth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in 1487, took up his fief at Anlu in 1494, and died in 1519. When his son later ascended the throne, he was posthumously honored as the Xian Emperor with the temple name Ruizong.

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Shen, You Kai, the Xianzong Emperor's fourteenth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Hongzhi with a residence established at Xuzhou Prefecture. He died in the sixteenth year before going to his fief. He had no sons; the enfeoffment was abolished.

translations.literal: The one who received enfeoffment was Prince Gong of Jing, Zai Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Only one received a princely title: Zhu Zaizhen as Prince Gong of Jing.

sentences.zh: 景 恭王載圳，世宗庶四子，嘉靖十八年封。四十年就藩德安府。四十四年薨。無子，封除。

translations.literal: Prince Gong of Jing, Zai Zhen, the Shizong Emperor's fourth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in the eighteenth year of Jiajing. In the fortieth year he went to his fief at De'an Prefecture. He died in the forty-fourth year. He had no sons; the enfeoffment was abolished.

translations.literal: Apart from Shenzong, the crown prince Xian and Huai and the other imperial sons died young.

translations.literal: The one who received enfeoffment was Prince Jian of Lu, Yi Liu.

translations.literal: Prince Jian of Lu, Yi Liu, the Muzong Emperor's fourth son by the principal consort, was enfeoffed in the fifth year of Longqing. In the seventeenth year of Wanli he went to his fief at Weihui Prefecture. He died in the forty-second year.

translations.literal: Prince Chang Fen, the Jian prince's only son by a secondary consort, succeeded in the forty-sixth year of Wanli. Later, when the dynasty fell, he lodged at Hangzhou. In the sixth month of the second year of Shunzhi, when the Qing army arrived, he surrendered.

translations.literal: Prince Gong of Fu, Chang Xun, the Shenzong Emperor's third son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli. In the forty-second year he went to his fief at Henan Prefecture. In the first month of the fourteenth year of Chongzhen, Li Zicheng's rebels took Luoyang and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong of Fu, Zhu Changxun, the Shenzong Emperor's third son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in 1601, took up his fief at Henan Prefecture in 1614, and was killed when Li Zicheng's rebels captured Luoyang in the first month of 1641.

sentences.zh: 由崧，恭庶一子，萬曆四十五年封德昌王。崇禎十六年襲封。十七年，闖賊陷京師，五月自立於南京，僭號弘光。大清順治二年五月，王師渡江，被執。

translations.literal: You Song, the Gong prince's only son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed as Prince of Dechang in the forty-fifth year of Wanli and succeeded in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen. In the seventeenth year, when Li Zicheng's rebels took the capital, in the fifth month he declared himself ruler at Nanjing with the reign title Hongguang. In the fifth month of the second year of Shunzhi, when the Qing army crossed the Yangzi, he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yousong, the Gong prince's only son by a secondary consort, was made Prince of Dechang in 1617 and inherited the main line in 1643. When Li Zicheng's rebels took Beijing in 1644, he declared himself emperor at Nanjing in the fifth month under the reign title Hongguang. In the fifth month of 1645, when Qing forces crossed the Yangzi, he was captured.

cells.content: 惠 王常潤，神宗庶六子，萬曆二十九年封。天啟七年就藩荊州府。崇禎末，奔廣州府。大清順治三年，廣東平，被執，死。

In the third year of Shunzhi, when Guangdong was pacified, he was captured and died.

In the seventh year of Tianqi he went to his fief at Hengzhou Prefecture. In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen, when Zhang Xianzhong's rebels took Hengzhou, the prince fled from Yongzhou into Guangxi and lodged at Cangwu. He died in the seventeenth year.

cells.content: 由𣜬，端嫡三子，初封安仁王。唐王聿鍵自立，偽封為桂王。大清順治三年，卒於梧州。無子。 由榔，端嫡四子，初封永明王。大清順治三年，福建平，由榔自立於肇慶，僭號永曆。是冬，王師度嶺，由榔走廣西，自是走貴州，又走雲南，遂入緬甸。十八年冬，王師至，緬人獻之。明年，殺諸雲南。

translations.literal: You [𣜬], the Duan prince's third son by the principal consort, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Anren. When the Tang prince Yujian declared himself ruler, he was falsely enfeoffed as Prince of Gui. He died at Wuzhou in the third year of Shunzhi without sons. You Lang, the Duan prince's fourth son by the principal consort, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yongming. In the third year of Shunzhi, when Fujian was pacified, You Lang declared himself ruler at Zhaoqing with the reign title Yongli. That winter, when the Qing army crossed the Lingnan passes, You Lang fled to Guangxi, then to Guizhou, then to Yunnan, and finally into Burma. In the winter of the eighteenth year, when the Qing army arrived, the Burmese handed him over. The next year he was executed in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu You[𣜬], the Duan prince's third son by the principal consort, was first made Prince of Anren and was falsely enfeoffed as Prince of Gui when the Tang prince Zhu Yujian declared himself emperor. He died at Wuzhou in 1646 without heirs. Zhu Youlang, the fourth son by the principal consort, was first made Prince of Yongming. In 1646, after Fujian was pacified, he declared himself emperor at Zhaoqing under the reign title Yongli. That winter Qing forces crossed into Lingnan; he fled through Guangxi, Guizhou, and Yunnan into Burma. cells.literal: You [𣜬], the Duan prince's third son by the principal consort, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Anren. When the Tang prince Yujian declared himself ruler, he was falsely enfeoffed as Prince of Gui. He died at Wuzhou in the third year of Shunzhi without sons. You Lang, the Duan prince's fourth son by the principal consort, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yongming. In the third year of Shunzhi, when Fujian was pacified, You Lang declared himself ruler at Zhaoqing with the reign title Yongli. That winter, when the Qing army crossed the Lingnan passes, You Lang fled to Guangxi, then to Guizhou, then to Yunnan, and finally into Burma. In the winter of the eighteenth year, when the Qing army arrived, the Burmese handed him over. The next year he was executed in Yunnan.

translations.literal: The Zhuanglie Emperor had seven sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Chongzhen Emperor had seven sons.

sentences.zh: 獻愍太子慈烺外，嫡第二子，庶第五子、第六子、第七子俱殤。

translations.literal: Apart from the crown prince Xian and Min, Cihuang, the second son by the principal consort and the fifth, sixth, and seventh sons by secondary consorts all died young.
translations.idiomatic: Besides the crown prince Cihuang, the second son by the principal consort and the fifth, sixth, and seventh sons by secondary consorts all died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 其封而未建藩邸者二王，曰定哀王慈炯，曰永悼王慈炤。

translations.literal: Two were enfeoffed but did not establish princely residences: Prince Ai of Ding, Cijiong, and Prince Dao of Yong, Cizhao.
translations.idiomatic: Two were enfeoffed but never established princely residences: Zhu Cijiong as Prince Ai of Ding and Zhu Cizhao as Prince Dao of Yong.

sentences.zh: 定 哀王慈炯，莊烈帝嫡三子，崇禎十四年封，未建藩邸。十七年，闖賊陷京師，被執，不知所終。

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Ding, Cijiong, the Zhuanglie Emperor's third son by the principal consort, was enfeoffed in the fourteenth year of Chongzhen without establishing a princely residence. In the seventeenth year, when Li Zicheng's rebels took the capital, he was captured and his fate is unknown.
